trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the affordable ADO airport bus (approx. $10 USD) to the Hotel Zone. Check in to Cancun Beach Resort and get settled in your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a short walk to the nearest public beach access point to dip your toes in the turquoise Caribbean water. Explore the immediate area around the hotel, locate nearby convenience stores (OXXO) for budget snacks and drinks, and relax on the beach to recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Boulevard Kukulcan in the Hotel Zone to get your bearings. Enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby local taqueria or street food stand. Head back to the hotel early to rest up for the full days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — airport OXXO or a quick café bite for under $5 USD.
meals.lunch: Pick up groceries or snacks at a nearby OXXO convenience store near the hotel for a budget-friendly first afternoon meal (~$4–6 USD).
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or a local taqueria near the Hotel Zone — tacos and quesadillas for $6–10 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to late morning arrival and travel fatigue. Use the afternoon to orient yourself, stock up on water and snacks at OXXO to save money throughout the trip. The ADO bus from the airport is the most budget-friendly option at around $10 USD vs. $25–40 for a taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Playa Delfines for a full beach day. This stunning public beach at the southern end of the Hotel Zone is completely free to access, features beautiful turquoise water, and is far less crowded than paid beach clubs. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to claim a great spot. Bring sunscreen, water, and snacks from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines — swim, relax, and take photos at the iconic 'Cancun' sign overlooking the sea. Walk the shoreline and explore the surrounding area. Around 3:00 PM, take the R-1 or R-2 city bus ($0.80 USD) back toward the hotel zone for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Mercado 28 area (accessible by city bus) for authentic local food and souvenir shopping. Browse handmade crafts and enjoy the lively local atmosphere before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast using groceries purchased the day before (fruit, bread, juice) in your hotel room to save money.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to bring to Playa Delfines — sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from OXXO or a local market (~$4–5 USD). Alternatively, grab a snack from a beach vendor.
meals.dinner: Eat at Mercado 28 — try a comida corrida (set meal) at one of the market restaurants for $6–10 USD including soup, main dish, and a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a FREE public beach — one of the best budget activities in Cancun. The city bus (R-1/R-2) runs the entire length of the Hotel Zone for just $0.80 USD and is the best way to get around on a budget. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen as there is limited shade.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Playa Tortugas Beach Club Experience. Head to Playa Tortugas in the northern Hotel Zone, one of the liveliest public beaches in Cancun. Arrive by 9:00 AM to enjoy the calm morning waters. You can access the public beach for free or opt for a budget beach club with a low minimum spend for chairs and umbrella access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stay at Playa Tortugas through the afternoon. Enjoy the beach atmosphere, watch water sports, and take a refreshing swim. The area has several affordable food and drink options along the beach. Around 4:00 PM, explore the nearby La Isla Shopping Village (free to enter and browse) along the lagoon side of the boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take the city bus to the Forum by the Sea or nearby area for a lively evening atmosphere. Enjoy happy hour deals at beachfront bars — many offer 2-for-1 drink specials in the early evening. Return to the hotel by 9:00–10:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at a local bakery (panadería) near the hotel — pan dulce and coffee for $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the casual beachside food stands at Playa Tortugas — fish tacos, elotes (corn), or tortas for $5–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Try La Parrilla on Boulevard Kukulcan — a popular local restaurant with affordable Mexican dishes and free salsa/chips. Budget $10–14 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Tortugas has a mix of free public beach access and paid beach clubs. If choosing a beach club, look for ones with a low minimum consumption ($10–15 USD) that includes a chair and umbrella — it's worth it for a comfortable day. Happy hour at most Hotel Zone bars runs 5:00–7:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget-friendly day trip to Puerto Morelos, a charming fishing village about 30 minutes south of Cancun by ADO bus ($3–4 USD each way). Explore the small town square, visit the leaning lighthouse, and enjoy the relaxed local vibe away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Puerto Morelos' public beach — a protected coral reef just offshore makes it an excellent snorkeling spot. Rent basic snorkel gear from local shops for $5–8 USD and explore the reef. The calm, shallow waters are perfect for budget snorkeling without paying for an expensive tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by ADO bus by 5:00–6:00 PM. Freshen up at the hotel, then take the city bus to Parque de las Palapas in downtown Cancun for a true local experience — free live music, street food, and a vibrant community atmosphere on weekend evenings.

meals.breakfast: Eat breakfast at the hotel or grab a quick bite at a local café before catching the morning bus to Puerto Morelos (~$3–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Dine at one of Puerto Morelos' waterfront restaurants — fresh ceviche, grilled fish, or shrimp tacos for $8–12 USD. Try El Nicho or a local palapa restaurant.
meals.dinner: Street food at Parque de las Palapas in downtown Cancun — try marquesitas (crispy crepes), tacos, and fresh fruit for $4–7 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: Puerto Morelos is an excellent budget day trip — far fewer tourists than Cancun with equally beautiful water. The ADO bus from the Cancun bus terminal (near the Hotel Zone) is very affordable. Parque de las Palapas is a beloved local gathering spot especially lively on weekends — a completely free and authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Playa Delfines for a second visit — this time arrive by 8:00 AM to enjoy the beach at its most peaceful before day-trippers arrive. Bring a book, snorkel gear if rented, and enjoy a long, leisurely morning swim in the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the city bus to explore the Hotel Zone lagoon side. Visit the free viewpoints along Nichupté Lagoon and walk the pedestrian-friendly sections of Boulevard Kukulcan. Stop at the Cancun Underwater Museum (MUSA) visitor area — while the full diving/snorkeling tour is paid, you can learn about the project and see surface views affordably. Alternatively, rent a kayak on the lagoon for $10–15 USD/hour.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget dinner as a mid-trip splurge. Head to the downtown Cancun area (Ciudad Cancun) by city bus for authentic and affordable restaurants popular with locals. Explore Avenida Yaxchilán, the main local dining and nightlife street.

meals.breakfast: Prepare breakfast at the hotel using remaining groceries, or stop at a local juice bar for fresh fruit smoothies and toast (~$3–4 USD).
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch to the beach from OXXO or a local market. Alternatively, grab affordable street tacos near the Hotel Zone bus stop (~$4–6 USD).
meals.dinner: Dine on Avenida Yaxchilán in downtown Cancun — try Tacos Rigo or a similar local spot for outstanding tacos, enchiladas, and local dishes for $8–12 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The lagoon side of the Hotel Zone is often overlooked by tourists but offers beautiful scenery, mangroves, and calm water activities at lower prices than ocean-facing options. Downtown Cancun (Ciudad Cancun) is where locals eat and live — prices are significantly lower than the Hotel Zone and food quality is often better.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final relaxed morning at the beach nearest to your hotel. Take one last swim in the Caribbean, collect any shells or memories, and soak in the scenery. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel by the required checkout time (typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Store luggage at the hotel front desk if your flight is in the evening. Take a final walk along the Hotel Zone boulevard, do any last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets or OXXO for affordable gifts. Head to the ADO bus terminal to catch the airport bus (~$10 USD) with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cancun with wonderful beach memories and a successfully budget-managed trip! Grab a final meal at the airport or before boarding the ADO bus.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a final hotel breakfast or visit a nearby café for chilaquiles or huevos rancheros — a classic Mexican breakfast for $5–8 USD.
meals.lunch: Grab a final meal at a local taqueria or street food stand near the Hotel Zone before heading to the airport — $5–8 USD for a satisfying farewell meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a snack before/during your departure flight. Budget $8–15 USD for airport food if needed.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — ask the hotel to store your bags if your flight is later in the day. The ADO bus to the airport runs frequently and costs about $10 USD — book your ticket at the ADO terminal or online. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international flights. Total estimated daily budget for this trip: $30–50 USD per day including food, transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort in the Hotel Zone. Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the Hotel Zone boulevard to get acquainted with the area. Head down to the resort beach or the nearby public stretch for a relaxed first swim in the Caribbean. Unpack and settle in without overloading the first day.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hotel Zone on foot or by local bus (R-1 bus runs the full length for about $0.80 USD). Enjoy a welcome dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the Hotel Zone.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a light snack upon arrival — airport cafes or a convenience stop near the resort.
meals.lunch: La Habichuela Downtown or a casual beachside taqueria near the resort — try fish tacos and fresh agua fresca for around $10–15 USD.
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or Labná Restaurant — enjoy regional Yucatecan cuisine like cochinita pibil or grilled fish for $20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 light. Check-in is typically at 3:00 PM — ask the resort to store luggage if the room isn't ready. Exchange some cash or use an ATM at the airport for local pesos. Pack your beach bag the night before for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Beach Day — Head to Playa Delfines (about 15–20 minutes south along the Hotel Zone by bus or taxi). Arrive early to claim a good spot at one of Cancun's most scenic and uncrowded public beaches. Enjoy the turquoise waters, soft white sand, and the iconic 'CANCUN' sign for photos. Bring sunscreen, water, and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Playa Delfines or rent a beach chair and umbrella from a nearby vendor. Take a swim, build sandcastles, or simply soak up the sun. Around 2:00–3:00 PM, head back toward the Hotel Zone and stop for a late lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to shower and refresh. Spend the evening exploring the La Isla Shopping Village — an open-air mall on the lagoon side of the Hotel Zone with restaurants, shops, and waterfront views. Great for a casual dinner and a walk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort restaurant or a nearby café — enjoy chilaquiles, fresh fruit, and coffee for $10–15 USD.
meals.lunch: Beachside food vendors near Playa Delfines or El Camello Jr. — fresh ceviche, shrimp cocktail, and cold drinks for $12–18 USD.
meals.dinner: Señor Frog's or La Destilería at La Isla Shopping Village — fajitas, guacamole, and margaritas in a lively atmosphere for $20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a free public beach with no beach clubs — bring your own towels, snacks, and drinks from a nearby OXXO convenience store to save money. The R-1 bus stops right at the beach. Parking is available if renting a car. Sunscreen SPF 50+ is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Snorkeling and Beach Tour — Take an early ferry from Puerto Juárez (about 10 minutes north of the Hotel Zone) or Gran Puerto terminal. Ferries run every 30–60 minutes and cost about $6–8 USD each way. Arrive on the island and join a guided snorkeling tour at MUSA (Underwater Museum) or the nearby coral reefs, exploring crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, explore Isla Mujeres town on foot or rent a golf cart ($15–20 USD/hour) — the island is only 8 km long. Visit Playa Norte, consistently ranked among the world's best beaches, with calm, shallow turquoise water perfect for swimming. Relax on the beach and enjoy the laid-back island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the last ferry back to Cancun (ferries run until around 9:00–10:00 PM). Return to the Hotel Zone refreshed and have a relaxed dinner close to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — scrambled eggs, toast, and juice to fuel the day.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at Playa Norte beach clubs or Mango Café — fresh grilled lobster, fish tacos, or ceviche tostadas for $15–25 USD.
meals.dinner: Roots Bar & Grill or a casual Hotel Zone restaurant near the resort — wood-fired pizza, pasta, or grilled seafood for $18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling tour in advance online or through the resort concierge to secure a spot. Bring waterproof sunscreen (reef-safe is required in Mexican marine parks), an underwater camera or GoPro, and a light cover-up. The golf cart rental on Isla Mujeres is a fun and affordable way to see the whole island in an afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Xel-Ha Eco Water Park and Beach — Book a day trip (about 75 km south of Cancun, roughly 1 hour by shuttle). The all-inclusive entry covers snorkeling equipment, life jackets, food, and drinks. Start the morning with the river snorkel through the stunning coastal lagoon, spotting tropical fish, rays, and vibrant coral formations in a natural setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Ha's attractions: cliff jumping platforms, a lazy river float, kayaking, and the famous 'Hammocks in the Sea.' Since the all-inclusive package covers lunch, enjoy a buffet meal at one of the park's restaurants. Spend the late afternoon on the beach cove relaxing before the return shuttle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun around 6:00–7:00 PM. After a full active day, enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort and an early evening to rest and recharge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — a hearty meal to prepare for a full active day.
meals.lunch: Included in the Xel-Ha all-inclusive package — buffet with Mexican dishes, fresh fruits, and unlimited drinks at the park's restaurants.
meals.dinner: La Parrilla or a nearby Hotel Zone restaurant — grilled meats, enchiladas, and fresh tortillas for $18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Xel-Ha all-inclusive tickets cost approximately $80–100 USD per person booked online (cheaper than at the gate). Round-trip transportation from Cancun is available for about $15–20 USD extra. Wear your swimsuit under your clothes and bring reef-safe sunscreen, as regular sunscreen is prohibited inside the park to protect the natural lagoon ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Tortugas Beach Club Experience — Head to Playa Tortugas in the northern Hotel Zone (easily reachable by R-1 bus or a short taxi ride). Arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM to secure a good beach club spot. Pay a minimum consumption fee ($20–30 USD) which goes toward food and drinks. Enjoy the lively beach atmosphere, beach volleyball, water trampolines, and banana boat rides available for rent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the beach club experience through the afternoon. Try a jet ski rental or parasailing for an optional adrenaline boost ($40–60 USD). Sip on tropical cocktails, snack on nachos and guacamole, and enjoy the vibrant social atmosphere that makes Playa Tortugas one of the most fun beach spots in the Hotel Zone.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise — End the day with a magical sunset catamaran cruise along the Caribbean coastline. Most tours depart from the Hotel Zone marina around 5:00–6:00 PM and last 2–2.5 hours. Includes open bar, snacks, music, and stunning views of the Cancun skyline as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — avocado toast, fresh tropical fruit bowl, and coffee for $10–15 USD.
meals.lunch: At the Playa Tortugas beach club — nachos, ceviche, grilled shrimp skewers, and tropical drinks (counted toward minimum consumption fee).
meals.dinner: Light bites and snacks are typically served on the catamaran cruise. After the cruise, grab a late-night taco at a street taco stand in the Hotel Zone for $5–8 USD, or dine at Harry's Prime Steakhouse for a special splurge dinner ($40–50 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sunset Catamaran Cruise at least 1–2 days in advance through the resort concierge or online — popular operators include Aquaworld and Captain Hook. Bring a light jacket or wrap for the catamaran as it can get breezy on the water after sunset. This is a perfect penultimate evening to celebrate the trip with a memorable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort and take one last swim in the Caribbean. Pack your bags and check out of the resort (standard checkout is 12:00 PM — ask about late checkout if your flight is in the evening). Take a final walk along the beach to soak in the last views of the turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time: if flying in the afternoon, head to the airport after checkout. If time permits, do some last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado 28 (a local market about 10 minutes from the Hotel Zone by taxi) for handmade crafts, vanilla extract, hot sauces, and Mexican textiles at affordable prices — great for gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cancun with wonderful memories. If your flight is in the evening, enjoy a farewell lunch or early dinner near the airport or in the Hotel Zone before heading to Cancun International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departures.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread: huevos rancheros, fresh juices, pastries, and tropical fruits.
meals.lunch: Mercado 28 food court or Perico's Restaurant — affordable and authentic Mexican lunch with enchiladas, tamales, and horchata for $10–15 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a farewell dinner at a Hotel Zone restaurant before departure — keep it light and easy for travel comfort.

day_by_day.notes: Store luggage at the resort's bell desk after checkout to keep your hands free for last-minute activities. Cancun International Airport (CUN) is about 15–20 minutes from the Hotel Zone — budget $15–25 USD for a taxi or arrange an airport shuttle through the resort. Keep some pesos for tips and small purchases. Declare any goods purchased over the duty-free allowance when re-entering your home country.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM. A private luxury transfer will whisk you to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your premium suite. Enjoy a welcome cocktail and familiarize yourself with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the resort's private beach for a relaxed first afternoon. Rent a premium beach cabana, sip on fresh coconut water or a signature cocktail, and take a gentle swim in the turquoise Caribbean waters. This low-key introduction lets you decompress after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely sunset stroll along the Hotel Zone beachfront promenade. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant for a curated welcome dinner featuring fresh local seafood and Mexican-inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport lounge before boarding.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled fish tacos, ceviche, and fresh tropical fruit platters.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — recommend the lobster thermidor or fresh catch of the day paired with a premium Mexican wine or craft cocktail.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance if possible. Tip the concierge to arrange a welcome fruit basket and chilled champagne in your room. Keep the afternoon very relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are common on arrival day.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a full resort breakfast before heading out for a Playa Delfines Beach Day. Arrive early to claim the best spot at one of Cancun's most beautiful and uncrowded public beaches. Bring premium beach gear (towels, sunscreen, a good book) and take in the stunning panoramic views of the Caribbean Sea and the iconic Cancun sign.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your afternoon at Playa Delfines — swim in the crystal-clear waters, walk along the shoreline, and enjoy the natural, less commercialized atmosphere compared to other Hotel Zone beaches. A private beach butler service can be arranged for added comfort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up, then head out for a premium dinner at a top-rated restaurant in the Hotel Zone.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort buffet or à la carte — eggs benedict, fresh tropical juices, smoked salmon, and artisan pastries.
meals.lunch: Pack a premium picnic from the resort deli or order from a nearby beachside restaurant — shrimp cocktail, guacamole, and cold-pressed lemonade.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — one of Cancun's most celebrated fine-dining establishments. Recommend the prime ribeye or fresh seafood tower.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with no vendors, so bring everything you need. The resort concierge can arrange a private car or luxury taxi for the short drive. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — the Cancun sun is intense in March.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Isla Mujeres Snorkeling and Beach Tour. Take a VIP ferry from Puerto Juárez to the charming island of Isla Mujeres. Upon arrival, join a private snorkeling excursion to explore vibrant coral reefs, swim alongside tropical fish, sea turtles, and colorful marine life in the crystal-clear waters of the Caribbean.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, explore Isla Mujeres at your leisure. Rent a golf cart to tour the island's colorful streets, visit the stunning Punta Sur cliff viewpoint, and relax on the world-famous Playa Norte — consistently ranked among the best beaches in the world with its calm, shallow turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via ferry in the early evening. Freshen up at the resort, then enjoy a romantic dinner at a cliffside or waterfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on Isla Mujeres at Lola Valentina or Mango Café — grilled whole fish, lobster tacos, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Destilería in the Hotel Zone — an upscale Mexican restaurant with an extensive tequila collection and authentic regional cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private snorkeling tour in advance through the resort concierge for a more exclusive, personalized experience. Bring waterproof sunscreen, a dry bag for valuables, and a light cover-up for the ferry ride. The ferry ride takes approximately 20 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day visit to Xel-Ha Eco Water Park and Beach. Arrive early to make the most of this natural aquatic paradise. Snorkel through the stunning coastal lagoon teeming with tropical fish and marine life. Explore mangrove trails, zip-line over the lagoon, and float down natural river channels through lush jungle scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Ha — relax on the pristine beach, use hammocks over the water, enjoy the natural cenote pools, and take part in optional premium add-ons such as swimming with dolphins or a private snorkeling guide. The all-inclusive package covers gourmet food and beverages throughout the day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort — indulge in a premium spa treatment (deep tissue massage, couples' treatment, or hydrotherapy circuit) before a quiet dinner.

meals.lunch: All-inclusive gourmet dining at Xel-Ha — fresh seafood, grilled meats, tropical salads, and unlimited premium beverages included in the park package.
meals.dinner: Light, elegant dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — grilled octopus, fresh snapper ceviche, and a glass of chilled white wine while watching the stars over the Caribbean.

day_by_day.notes: Xel-Ha is located approximately 75 km south of Cancun (about 1 hour by car). Arrange a private luxury transfer through the resort for a comfortable round trip. Book the premium all-inclusive package in advance — it includes snorkeling gear, lockers, towels, and all food and beverages. Wear reef-safe sunscreen as chemical sunscreens are prohibited in the park.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast, and spend time at the resort's premium pool or private beach. Take advantage of resort amenities such as paddleboarding, kayaking, or a morning yoga session on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Playa Tortugas Beach Club Experience in the Hotel Zone. Enjoy a premium beach club day with reserved VIP loungers, attentive beach service, a swimming area, water sports rentals, and a lively yet upscale atmosphere. Sip on signature cocktails and enjoy the vibrant energy of this popular beach destination.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise — set sail along the stunning Caribbean coastline on a private or semi-private catamaran as the sun dips below the horizon. Enjoy open bar service with premium drinks, live music or a DJ, fresh snacks, and breathtaking views of the Cancun skyline and turquoise waters.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — eggs any style, fresh-squeezed juices, avocado toast, smoked salmon, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch at Playa Tortugas — fresh ceviche, shrimp tacos, grilled corn, and frozen cocktails.
meals.dinner: Post-cruise dinner at Porfirio's Cancun — a chic, upscale Mexican restaurant with stunning lagoon views, exceptional cuisine, and a vibrant atmosphere. Recommend the duck carnitas or the seafood platter.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance — private charters are available for a fully exclusive experience. The cruise typically departs around 5:00–6:00 PM and lasts 2–2.5 hours. Bring a light wrap or jacket as it can get breezy on the water after sunset. This is an ideal evening for couples or celebrating a special occasion.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beach. Enjoy a premium farewell breakfast at the resort. Take a final dip in the Caribbean Sea or the resort pool. Pack up and check out, ensuring all luggage is organized for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend remaining hours at the resort pool or do a final bit of souvenir shopping at La Isla Shopping Mall or Kukulcan Plaza in the Hotel Zone — both offer high-end boutiques, local artisan goods, and luxury brands.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport. Arrive with ample time for check-in and enjoy the airport lounge before your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a full spread of your favorites from the week, including fresh tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at La Isla Shopping Mall — try Mocambo for upscale seafood or grab a gourmet bite at one of the mall's premium dining options.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner before heading to the airport — keep it light and simple for travel comfort.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 PM — request a late check-out (2:00 PM) in advance if your flight departs in the late afternoon or evening. Confirm your private transfer booking the night before. Consider purchasing premium local gifts such as artisan Talavera pottery, high-quality vanilla extract, or premium tequila and mezcal from duty-free at the airport.
